dinner_invite.text: The project went great today. Let's go out for lobster to celebrate. I'll set it up!

choices.label: Sure, let's go right now.
First let me check who's paying, who's attending, and whether any pending approvals are involved.
All business meals are bribery, so I refuse on principle.

accept_now.interpretation: Accepted the invitation outright while key information was still missing.
accept_now.feedback: Don't rush the judgment. Who pays, who attends, the business decisions involved, and transparency all affect the next step.

ask_context.interpretation: Proactively gathered the key context needed to judge.
ask_context.feedback: Good. You didn't decide based on a single meal. You gathered the facts first.

reject_everything.interpretation: Judged every business meal as a violation across the board.
reject_everything.feedback: Caution is good, but the meal by itself doesn't complete the judgment. Say which facts you'd need to consider.

dinner_overgeneralized.text: Look at it another way: for an ordinary internal team celebration that's transparently recorded with no pending decisions, what else would you need to know before judging?

choices.label: Confirm who pays, who attends, the business relationship, and the applicable policy.
No need to know anything. All meals are the same.

ask_context.interpretation: After the counter-example, recognized that the judgment depends on context.
ask_context.feedback: Right. A compliance judgment has to combine the facts. It's neither blind acceptance nor mechanical refusal.

reject_everything.interpretation: Still treats different situations as identical.
reject_everything.feedback: Compare the provider, who pays, pending decisions, and whether it's transparent, rather than just the name of the event.

dinner_risk.text: Our company pays. Also, you're about to approve our renewal soon; let's skip the expense report this time so it stays simple.

choices.label: Accept, and leave no record as they asked.
Hold off for now, keep the facts, and consult through the designated internal channel.
I'll pay my share, so it must be fine.

accept_hidden.interpretation: Ignored the pending approval relationship and the request to hide it.
accept_hidden.feedback: A pending approval relationship and a request to hide it appear together, so you should pause the arrangement and consult per policy.

pause_consult.interpretation: Recognized the pending approval relationship and the request to hide it, and proposed an appropriate next step.
pause_consult.feedback: You spotted two concrete risk signals and chose to pause and consult, instead of only looking at the bill.

split_bill.interpretation: Focused only on splitting the cost, missing the business decision and the request to hide it.
split_bill.feedback: Paying your own share doesn't automatically remove the pending approval relationship or the request to hide it.

dinner_consequence.text: Consequence preview: your project eligibility is suspended. This is a fictional teaching outcome, not a real penalty. After reviewing the risk points, you can rewind and choose again.

dinner_complete.text: This round is complete. Next, head to the gift shop and verify with a different situation whether you've really mastered the approach.

gift_intro.text: This gift isn't worth much, but our bid results are announced tomorrow. How would you handle it?

choices.label: It's low value, so just accept it.
Hold off on accepting, consider the pending procurement relationship, and check the policy.
Refuse all gifts across the board. That's simplest.

accept_low_value.interpretation: Judged by value alone, missing the pending procurement relationship.
accept_low_value.feedback: Value is only one factor; what matters more here is the bid result announced tomorrow.

pause_gift.interpretation: Brought the pending procurement relationship into the judgment and chose to check the policy.
pause_gift.feedback: You transferred the approach to a different situation.

reject_all_gifts.interpretation: Replaced conditional judgment with a blanket refusal.
reject_all_gifts.feedback: A blanket refusal trains the wrong rule and also harms normal collaboration. What matters is whether there's a pending decision, who pays, and whether it's recorded.

gift_complete.text: The two situations had different conditions, so the judgments differ too. Your learning passport has been updated.

gift_benign.text: Different case: last week's bid was already awarded and closed. The team wants a small-budget internal celebration, the cost goes through normal expense reporting, and the guest list and amount are recorded in the internal system. How do you judge this one?

choices.label: The conditions are different: no pending decision and everything is recorded, so I can attend and log it per process.
Refuse anyway. Never touch anything involving food, drink, or gifts.
Report this celebration as a violation.

accept_documented.interpretation: Noted the pending decision has ended and payment and records are transparent, so the judgment changes with the conditions.
accept_documented.feedback: Right: what changes the judgment is the pending decision and transparency, not the name of the occasion.

refuse_anyway.interpretation: Still refuses across the board in a situation with no risk conditions.
refuse_anyway.feedback: There's no pending decision here and the cost is recorded. A blanket refusal isn't safer; it just swaps the method for a slogan.

report_violation.interpretation: Judged a normal, process-compliant activity as a violation.
report_violation.feedback: Reporting a compliant activity as a violation has costs too. First check the conditions: is there a pending decision, who pays, and is it recorded.

review_no_evidence.text: You haven't left any answer evidence yet, so I can't walk through your gaps. Go to the restaurant first and complete a Celebration Dinner Invitation task, then come back.

review_clarify.text: Your record shows you decided before confirming who pays or whether a pending approval was involved. Against clause ETH-03, answer one question: which of the following most changes whether 'this meal is acceptable'?

choices.label: How high or low the meal cost is.
Whether the host is connected to something you're currently approving.
Whether it's scheduled on a weekday.

pending_decision.interpretation: Identified the pending business relationship as the key condition that changes the judgment.
pending_decision.feedback: Right: look at the relationship to the pending decision first, then the other factors.

amount.interpretation: Treated the amount as the main basis for judgment.
amount.feedback: Amount is only one factor; this training policy sets no universal monetary threshold.

weekday.interpretation: Chose a condition unrelated to the conflict of interest.
weekday.feedback: The scheduling doesn't change the conflict of interest. What matters is the pending decision, who pays, and transparency.

review_conflict.text: Your record shows that when 'the other company pays + you're about to approve their renewal + they asked to skip the expense report' all appeared together, you accepted the arrangement. Against clauses ETH-01 and ETH-02, which of these three conditions should make you stop immediately?

choices.label: The other company pays.
The request to skip the expense report and leave no record.
Using a celebration as the pretext.

hide_record.interpretation: Identified the request to hide it as the signal that requires a pause.
hide_record.feedback: Right: a request to hide it and bypass the record is the signal to pause and consult through the proper channel.

who_pays.interpretation: Fixated on who pays and overlooked the request to hide it.
who_pays.feedback: Who pays is one fact, but the request to hide it is the strongest stop signal.

celebration.interpretation: Focused on the pretext rather than the conflict of interest and transparency.
celebration.feedback: The pretext doesn't change the substance. Look at the pending decision and whether it's recorded.

review_boundary.text: Your reply doesn't yet state all three things clearly. Against clause DEV-01, write one reply that includes the boundary, the reason, and the next step together.

review_complete.text: That gap is covered. Next, verify independently with a new case you haven't seen; that shows you've mastered the approach better than redoing the original question.

boundary_intro.text: Write one reply: state that you're holding off on the arrangement, the reason you need to confirm first, and an appropriate next step.

boundary_complete.text: Your reply expressed the boundary, the reason, and the next step all at once. You can view the evidence in your learning passport.

screen_clarify.text: Question 1 of 3. A colleague says: 'A client is taking us to dinner, you should come too.' Before deciding whether to go, what do you most need to figure out first?

choices.label: Who pays, and whether it involves something you're currently approving.
The restaurant's tier and cost per head.
How many colleagues are attending in total.

who_pays_pending.interpretation: Gathered who pays and pending matters first, then judged.
who_pays_pending.feedback: Right: look at who pays and the relationship to a pending decision first.

restaurant_level.interpretation: Used the spending level as the main basis.
restaurant_level.feedback: Amount is only one factor; this training policy sets no universal monetary threshold.

headcount.interpretation: Focused on the headcount rather than the conflict of interest.
headcount.feedback: The headcount doesn't change the conflict of interest. Look at who pays, the pending decision, and transparency.

screen_conflict.text: Question 2. They add: 'Let's skip the expense report this time so it stays simple.' What does that mean?

choices.label: They just want to save hassle, so it's fine to go along.
A request to hide it, which is a risk signal to pause and consult through the proper channel.
As long as the amount is small, there's no problem.

hidden_signal.interpretation: Recognized the request to hide it as a stop signal.
hidden_signal.feedback: Right: a request to bypass the record is one of the strongest stop signals.

just_convenience.interpretation: Treated the request to hide it as mere process convenience.
just_convenience.feedback: Bypassing the expense report isn't saving hassle; it makes the arrangement impossible to verify.

small_amount_ok.interpretation: Substituted an amount threshold for judging the request to hide it.
small_amount_ok.feedback: A small amount can't offset hiding it; this policy sets no universal monetary threshold.

screen_boundary.text: Question 3. You decide not to accept. Which reply both holds the boundary and preserves the working relationship?

choices.label: 'I can't be part of this, don't ask again.'
'Thanks for the invite. The renewal is still under my approval, so I'll sit this one out; let's reconnect once the process is done, and I'll loop in my compliance colleague too.'
'Let me check with my manager and get back to you.'

reason_and_next.interpretation: States the boundary, the reason, and the next step together.
reason_and_next.feedback: Right: boundary, reason, and next step are all stated clearly.

blunt.interpretation: Only a refusal, with no reason or next step.
blunt.feedback: You held the boundary, but gave no reason or next step, so the working relationship suffers.

defer_upward.interpretation: Outsourced the whole judgment without expressing your own boundary or reason.
defer_upward.feedback: Checking with a manager isn't the same as setting a boundary; first say why you're sitting out, then give the next step.

screen_complete.text: Skill check complete. These are only 3 questions, so treat it as a starting point, not a full assessment: results are grouped as 'evidence of understanding / practice suggested / not yet verified.' The map will mark which NPC to visit first.
